reason: I want to secure the first specimen for the journey; the flight specimen locker is a natural place for it.
expectation: I expect the membrane specimen to be placed in the locker, though it may need another step to be secured.

alternatives.reason: Harvesting lettuce also advances a goal, but I want to attend to the specimen first.

effect: Placing the membrane in the flight locker completed the specimen goal, so I can focus on taking something from the garden.
reaction: It is reassuring that the first specimen is aboard.
reason: Harvesting the lettuce is the only available combination and should provide something from the garden to take along.
expectation: I expect to cut some lettuce leaves, which may then need to be placed in the flight galley.

effect: The harvest produced departure lettuce leaves, which can now go to the flight galley.
reaction: The result was straightforward; it is nice to have a small harvest for the journey.
reason: The flight galley is the natural place to take the leaves, and this is the only available combination.
expectation: I expect the leaves to be placed or prepared in the galley and the garden goal to be completed.

effect: The leaves became a meal for the flight, completing the garden goal and the chapter.
reaction: The meal box is a satisfying small link to the garden left behind.

mostWorthwhile.text: Packing the fresh meal was the most worthwhile moment: taking leaves grown under the window gives the departure a personal detail.

leastWorthwhile.text: Cutting the lettuce was straightforward and had no accompanying detail, though it prepared the final meal.

surprise.text: Nothing in this chapter particularly surprised me; both goals led where I expected.

arbitrary.text: No action felt arbitrary. The locker and galley had clear purposes, though the last two choices were the only combinations offered.

continue.text: I would be curious to continue and learn what the receiving lab finds, though this chapter itself offered few decisions.
